text:
sarah_p: Hey team — customer `payex-prod` reported sudden quality regression after an auto-failover to EU-standby. They saw hallucinations and truncated multilingual replies. Request IDs: r-8a3f4b and r-8a3f4c. Started ~14:02 UTC.

mike_ops: Thanks — is this the auth-probe failover we saw earlier? Any evidence the model variant changed?

sarah_p: They pasted the response which switched from `redwood-xxl-v2` to `redwood-xxl-lite-quant`. Outputs included garbled German and missing sections. They also saw a billing jump (extra tokens) around the same time.

raj_infra: Looking at routing logs for those req ids — the region routing for their tenant hit EU-standby due to auth probe timeout against NA; fallback policy picked a compatible-architecture variant but different tokenizer/profile.

iris_support: Customer provided a curl repro. Pasting sanitized snippet:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" -d '{"model":"redwood-xxl-v2","input":"Bitte fasse das Dokument zusammen:"}'
```

sarah_p: When run during the incident we got: `model_served: redwood-xxl-lite-quant` and output: "ZusammenfaÃung..." (broken umlauts).

mike_ops: That points to tokenizer vocab mismatch or encoding difference between variants. Also billing-bot shows a burst of token billing at 14:02 for that tenant — likely because lite-quant expanded tokens unexpectedly.

billing-bot: Alert: tenant payex-prod usage +23% tokens between 14:00-14:10 UTC. Charge bump flagged.

raj_infra: Repro steps I used from inside the EU standby network: 1) Force auth probe to fail against NA control plane (iptables drop). 2) Send identical request. Observed immediate fallback to `redwood-xxl-lite-quant`. Routing decision excerpt: `policy: region-prefer -> fallback: compatible-arch -> variant: lite-quant`

raj_infra: Quick check: lite-quant uses a shared tokenizer family with a different vocab file and BPE offsets — that'll produce mojibake for some multi-byte chars.

iris_support: Customer impact: summaries missing paragraphs and non-ASCII characters corrupted. They depend on German output for invoices. Escalation requested to SE and billing review.

mike_ops: Short-term mitigation: 1) Pin their tenant routing to `region: na` or `model_override: redwood-xxl-v2` until we fix mismatch. 2) Block auto-fallback to variants that don't share tokenizer family.

sarah_p: Customer asked if we can rollback charges from the token spike — billing linked the spike to the failover window.

billing-bot: Please open billing dispute with evidence: request ids, timestamps, and routing logs. I tagged invoice INV-2026-093 for review.

raj_infra: Engineering action items I propose: 
- Add a compatibility matrix for tokenizer/vocab families to routing policy so fallback requires tokenizer compatibility.
- Add token-estimation guard — if variant is quantized-lite and token count delta > threshold, abort fallback.
- Emit explicit `served_variant` header in responses to help debugging.

mike_ops: I'm going to push a temporary routing rule to exempt `payex-prod` from auto-fallback and pin model to `redwood-xxl-v2` in eu-west config. Will notify when done.

oncall-bot: @raj_infra assigned incident #INC-2026-201 to investigate variant-tokenizer drift. SLA impact <1 min but customer impact moderate.

iris_support: Sarah, can you ask customer to run the attached test harness? They should set `X-Force-Standby: true` and paste the `served_variant` header value.

sarah_p: Sent to customer. They replied: `served_variant: redwood-xxl-lite-quant` and attached example output.

mike_ops: Done pinning rule for payex-prod. Confirmed subsequent requests -> `redwood-xxl-v2`. Customer reports German text restored.

sarah_p: Customer appreciates the quick fix but wants long-term guarantee.

raj_infra: Roadmap items: tokenizer-aware failover policy, fallback token-estimation, and dashboard alerting for variant drift. I'll open PRs and link to the incident.

iris_support: Billing dispute opened. SE assigned to coordinate contract credits.

sarah_p: Closing loop — customer will monitor for 24h. Will re-open if any regression. Thanks everyone :heart: 

mike_ops: Follow-up: log entry to add for future threads: `served_variant`, `tokenizer_family`, `routing_reason` — that would make root-cause much faster.

raj_infra: Agree. Also adding unit test to routing policy to prevent incompatible-tokenizer fallback.

billing-bot: Billing dispute submitted. Reference: DIS-2026-77.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-201 status -> resolved (mitigated by pinning).
